text:
A kinetic group needs no name; its shared constants do. They are fitted parameters, so they need names that users read in fitted_params, in the printed law and in identify's CSVs. Each constant is named after one member step, the group's naming representative. A group of A bindings at E and at E(B) that shares one K is called K_EA_to_E_A or K_EAB_to_EB_A, depending on which member names it.

It matters in two ways:
- Today it changes dedup. identify's eq_hash hashes the printed equation with its names, so the same model written with different groupings gets a different hash (327 of 663 regroupings in the probes) and is fitted twice.
- After the rewrite the key is computed from content, so names affect neither dedup nor values. What is left is readability and stability: the same model written two ways should report the same names, so results and tests compare.

E3 is about that stability. Today's rule picks the representative by rendered names, the joint solve then keeps a possibly different member's column, and regrouping the same model changes which member names the class (9.4% of same-model regroupings in the slice). Naming each class after the member the solve keeps makes the names a function of the model alone; it renames 2% of fitted names once. Unnamed constants (K1, K2, …) would also be stable, but unreadable.
